name: Holderness School Corner
beta: Alternate between stemming, laybacking and plain face climbing as you work up the corner on the flake to the shared anchor.
overview: A fun route up the corner that a large flake forms on its left side, ending at the anchor shared with its neighbor.

current.descent: (no DESCENT section on this route's page)
current.anchor: shares the 2-bolt anchor of Holderness School Arete

name: Hotter Than Hell
beta: On the first pitch, climb the face to a bolt over a little roof, then work rightward past a second bolt and a crack angling left. Edge and smear across the sloping slab above, clipping further bolts, up to a delicate crux under a triangular niche. Belay there if rope drag builds, or keep going.
overview: A well-protected bolted face line, found by scrambling over the ledge beside Inferno Corner. Edging and smearing past a series of bolts leads to a thin crux below a triangular niche. Often linked with a later pitch of Tranquility.

current.area_walk_in: Follow the yellow-blazed trail left past the first golf tees as it curves around the South Buttress. At a small cairn, take the climbers' path to the right and climb steeply to the base of the big slab, then traverse right along its foot and scramble up its left side to reach the routes.
current.descent: Two double-rope rappels off trees
current.location: Ledge leads left from Inferno Corner; the line begins where Tranquility Slab starts

name: Juan Valdez
beta: Scramble around rightward to a belay perch, then lieback and undercling the left-slanting flake system under the overhang. Work up a sharp arete on edges, pass a tight corner facing left, and finish through a headwall to the anchors set at the lip.
overview: Lieback and undercling a leftward, overhanging flake, then edge a sharp arete and a tight corner to a final headwall.

current.area_walk_in: A brief hillside trail climbs up to the cliff's foot.
current.descent: (no DESCENT section on this route's page)
current.location: From a belay ledge gained by scrambling around to the right

name: Jugline
beta: Pumpy moves lead up the leaning wall past three bolts; stretching far right and then returning left keeps the difficulty down. Above, an easy slab runs to anchors beside a hanging block.
overview: Tiring moves on an overhanging wall, with a long stretch right then back left that keeps the grade down, followed by a gentle slab up to the anchors.

current.area_walk_in: Follow the Waimea path to the Darth Vader junction, bear right beyond the fork for the Id's monster crag, and keep ascending. It is easy to overlook at first. A second path traverses eastward out of Waimea, arriving above the crag.

name: Livin' Astro
beta: Follow That Crack for the first 20 feet, then shift left and crank up the overhanging black arete to the high anchors.
overview: One of the region's hardest lines: after a short crack start it steps left and powers up a steep black arete.

current.area_walk_in: Follow the roadside path from the lot, climb the steep steps to the hillside trail, and angle uphill past the Bonsai wall to arrive at the right side of Waimea. It is a stiff half-hour climb.

current.location: Shares the first 20 ft of That Crack, then moves left onto the black arete

name: Razor Crack
beta: Pitch one aids the vertical crack, which leans out slightly and bulges near the top, up toward the belay spot; most of it is fixed. Pitch two ends along a slim crack. Pins and nuts, in modest numbers, make up the rack.
overview: A perfect aid crack splitting the Right Roof, an unmistakable line, with a slim crack for the final stretch.

current.area_walk_in: Take the Boulder Loop Trail to the point where the loop splits and bear right; the cliff soon appears beside you, rising above a talus slope.
current.location: The obvious crack splitting the Right Roof.

name: Man Overboard
beta:
Begin up Technosurfing: a corner facing left leads to the broken band of rock, and from there you traverse over to chains on a ledge. Clip in, then haul the rope off the lower bolts so it doesn't drag higher up.

Pull over a bulge into an open corner, work leftward then back right to the foot of the huge roof near the clifftop, and swing across exposed jugs onto a pumped-out lip and the dangling anchors.
overview: A crazy, airy route through the wall's centre toward the huge roof: a corner reaches the fractured band, a rightward traverse gains chains on a shelf, then come a bulge, an open-book corner, and a jug-hauling swing across the roof to anchors dangling past the edge.

name: Masterpiece
beta: Climb the short corner (a medium cam protects it) and continue on buckets through the leaning wall into a broken zone. Above, edge your way up a gentler open book, sitting on the roof's left, to reach the anchors.
overview: A popular line that begins in a small corner, then climbs bucket holds through an overhanging section and a broken area beside a big roof.

name: Peer Pressure
beta: Use good edges to head up and right inside the overhanging corner, with fun laybacks around a flake leading to the rim. The anchors are off to the left.
overview: A superb Rumney line that begins beneath a huge, right-slanting, left-facing dihedral at the left end of the Bonsai crag.

name: Red Sea Pedestrian
beta: Face climb past the bolts, getting across a small roof partway, and continue to the anchor.

name: Restless Native
beta:
Find the obviously overhanging crack system. Work leftward along a slanting seam of lumpy rock, then wrestle over a big flake to a straddling rest on top of it. A tricky corner facing right, with two bolts, leads to a hands-free head-jam rest.

Above that, pinch holds, laybacks and kneebars carry you up the pumpy flake system to a ledge from which to clip the chain anchor.
overview: A long, varied line: chunky rock and a big flake lead to a right-facing corner, then a pumpy overhanging flake system with a famous head-jam rest.

beta: Follow great edges up the outer side of the pillar, and carry a mid-sized cam to protect the crack beyond the second bolt.
overview: Great rock with edges up the outer face of a pillar; a medium cam helps in the crack above the second bolt.

name: Social Climber
beta: Face climb for about twenty feet past three bolts, then head leftward into a crack lodged behind the flake. Edge rightward beneath the slanting corner to the lip anchors. A small tech Friend is useful.
overview: A Bonsai line starting beside the obvious hanging arete, then following a crack hidden behind a flake, finishing under a corner that leans right.

name: Social Distortion
beta: Begin at the ramp's lower-left end and climb easy rock until the initial bolt. Powerful moves on overhanging rock follow, then you pull onto a rest. Work leftward on jugs and finally back right to the chains at the lip.
overview: A powerful Bonsai line that starts on easy ground, turns steep and overhanging past the first bolt, and ends at lip anchors after a rest.

name: Technosurfing
beta: An awkward, shallow corner facing left takes you to a first rest, then you head up and left across a pumpy, cool-looking bulge to another good rest. Technical, easier rock finishes at the anchor on the horizontal break.
overview: A crag classic mixing hard moves with good rests: a shallow corner, a pumpy bulge, then technical but easier ground to the break.

name: Lucifer in Chains
beta: Work a bolt-protected bouldery sequence along the outer left margin of the cave.
overview: A short, bolted line that plays like a hard boulder problem on the outside left lip of the steep granite cave.

current.area_walk_in: A woodland path running between the Cote Boulder and the Practice Slab leads to the cave.

name: Thin Air
beta: Start slightly left where it is easier, or ascend directly on solid holds for roughly fifty feet, arriving at a two-bolt stance. The second pitch is a long traverse rightward; use whatever fixed gear is there and look after your second.
overview: A hugely popular moderate up the middle of a pale granite face, with positive holds and a long rightward traverse where the second needs protecting.

current.descent: Do not rap the line itself: two double-rope raps down the face to its left, or walk off right along the tree ledge
current.location: Starts where the rock first breaks up, around 150 ft uphill of Standard Route

name: Thinner
beta: Find the thin corner that faces right, down and right from where Thin Air begins. Traverse up and right over shelves and rubbly granite until you stand left of the bottom of the corner, climb its right face until you can step left, then continue up its outer arete past a pair of short headwalls to the chains.
overview: Fine face climbing up a corner's right wall and outside edge to short headwalls; protection is poor, so many toprope it.

name: Tsunami
beta:
A delicate bouldery opening leads about twelve feet to an eyebolt under a short corner facing right. Rock over onto the ledge, then climb the fractured whitish band, passing through an inverted V up toward a roof.

Undercling under the roof, clip the bolt past its lip, pull over, trend up a leaning slab, then finish leftward on an arete to anchors at a stance.
overview: Varied climbing: a tricky start, a band of pale rock, an inverted V into a roof, then a steep slab and arete to finish.

name: Vallee Daze
beta: Leave the ledge beside the prominent arete and reach the first bolt, then transfer to the arete's other face using layback and crimp holds past five more bolts.
overview: A New Wave sport route up an arete, starting from a ledge and moving to its right side to lieback and crimp.

current.descent: lower off the fixed anchor
current.location: Off a ledge left of the prominent arete, then onto the arete's right side after the first bolt

name: War and  Peace
beta: Pull over a series of bulges on good holds, ending at anchors above a tight corner.
overview: Constantly engaging moves over a series of bulges on good holds, ending at anchors above a narrow corner.

name: Windfall
beta:
Start down and right of Thin Air, where a corner angles right. Take the easy flake for a few moves rightward, then trend leftward by a fixed piton toward a long, slim roof.

The crux is edging over that roof. Move up the face toward a fixed pin, mantle onto a bolt above, and angle left by a few more pegs to the belay stance.
overview: Strong face climbing past fixed pins and a narrow roof, with an unnerving runout mantle; often toproped.

name: South Buttress Direct
beta: The first pitch is the access ledge shared with The Eliminate. On pitch two, start from the tree ledge immediately left of that route, ascend a flake and aid-climb five bolts across a featureless wall toward a belay ledge. The third pitch follows a lengthy upright corner at left.
overview: First climbed solo in winter, it has since become a lengthy free route with a growing following. After the access ledge pitch, a flake leads to a blank wall that is aided on five bolts, and an extended upright corner finishes the route.

name: Yellow Zonkers
beta: Around the bend left of Wedged, a right-facing corner contains a chimney narrow enough to squeeze. Squirm your way to the pinnacle's summit, then face climb to descend from it.
overview: Squirm up a squeeze chimney in a right-facing corner to the top of a pinnacle.

current.area_walk_in: A vague path starts at the Lower Slab's left side and climbs to the cliff. You can also pass through the Summit Boulder Area, continue toward Locomotive Breath, and branch right to arrive at the cliff's far-right extremity.

name: Yoda
beta: Haul on buckets across bulges, clipping three bolts, until you reach a solid rest. Above that, edge your way up a steep, slabby wall whose rock has vertical strata.
overview: Fun moderate: big holds over bulges to a rest after the third bolt, then edging on a steeper slab with vertical bands.

current.area_walk_in: A compact steep crag capped by a giant roof, sitting about a hundred feet from the Darth Vader trail junction, on the left.

name: April Showers
beta: The hard part comes immediately, a bouldery sequence to a low ceiling. Then angle off leftward by a bolt to the stance. Parties can lower from there, or tackle the big overhang higher up by working out to the right.
overview: A bouldery opening sequence up to a low ceiling is the hard part, then a move left beside a bolt leads to a belay. From there most parties rappel, or continue out right over the large roof above to easier rock.

current.descent: rappel from the belay, or climb the big roof above to easier ground

name: Dick's Prick
beta: The original way up this spire follows the north-facing front side to the summit. Getting down is by rappel.
overview: The first line up this detached spire, it ascends the front face on the north side to the summit.

current.descent: rappel

name: Little Finger
beta: The slab is gentle enough that you can set up a belay almost anywhere. The continuous crack takes gear the full length, so stop wherever suits the party.
overview: The simplest route up a long low-angle slab, following a clear finger crack in its middle. It is a pleasant climb with continuous protection.

current.location: middle of the slab, along the finger-width crack, a short scramble right of the lake landing

name: Missing, But Not Lost
beta: Get up the right-facing dihedral on the left of its famous neighbor to the ledge, where the hardest move is. From there you can rappel off or continue on a separate easier route to the summit.
overview: A short corner leading to a ledge, where the hard part lies. Most parties stop there and rappel, or carry on by the neighboring route to finish.

current.area_walk_in: From the Uberfall follow the Undercliff carriage path beyond High Exposure; after a trailside block with a small overhang and a large dead-topped pine, turn up a yellow-blazed side path through talus to level ground below two large open corners.

name: Psychedelic (pitches 2 & 3 only)
beta: From the ledge, pull a roof at a corner, then traverse a long way right along horizontal cracks; a medium cam helps there. Then continue upward to the finish, and look after the follower on the traverse with good placements.
overview: Upper pitches of a line on the left side of the High E buttress: from the ledge, pull over the corner roof, then trend well right on horizontal cracks to the summit. The traverse deserves solid protection for the follower.

name: Strictly From Nowhere
beta: On the second pitch go up into the corner that faces left, and trend rightward onto a face with a tree plus a rappel station with bolts, a popular belay. To go on, angle left beyond a small overhang, then back right beyond another to a comfortable belay ledge.
overview: A fun route featuring a thrilling crux section and a pleasant finish. The crux can be linked diagonally into the key pitch on a nearby roof climb for a highly recommended combination.

current.area_walk_in: From the lot past the Visitor Center, take the stone-stepped connector trail up to the carriage road, then turn onto the access trail at the Strictly junction. The first wall is directly above; the roofs are just around the arete to the right.
current.descent: walk off left on the trail (rappelling the route is possible)
current.location: just left of where the connector trail meets the cliff, at the centre of a narrow rock toe roughly twenty feet across

name: Hurwal Divide Traverse
beta: Sacajawea Peak: from the head of Thorp Creek, climb steep fell fields and talus to the ridge and follow it to the summit, the high point of the range, on pale marble and limestone. Sacajawea to the Matterhorn: the crest south carries a handful of gendarmes; stay on the spine for Class 3 moves with moderate exposure, or drop onto the west side in scree to get around them. Expect to pick a line and backtrack at times. The Matterhorn: a broad white limestone summit, easy once you reach it. Back north onto the Hurwal Divide: return toward Sacajawea and turn east along the dog-legged divide, mostly on the right-hand (south/east) side of the crest to avoid exposure, over miles of crumbling shale, talus and scree with goat paths giving occasional relief, to the Hurwal Divide high point. Hurwal Divide to Chief Joseph Mountain: descend about two miles to a saddle, then follow the Chief Joseph ridge north over several intermediate points to the dark basalt summit cap of Chief Joseph Mountain.
overview: A long, off-trail loop along the high crest of the Wallowas, linking Sacajawea Peak and the Matterhorn to Chief Joseph Mountain by way of the Hurwal Divide and crossing about nine summits over 9,000 feet. Most of it is Class 2 talus and goat-path walking on loose, mixed rock, with short Class 3 scrambling around gendarmes between Sacajawea and the Matterhorn. There is no trail on the crest, no water on the ridge, and the finish is a hard bushwhack back down to Hurricane Creek.

current.approach: From Hurricane Creek Trailhead, walk the Hurricane Creek Trail about 1.8 miles to the unsigned, unmaintained Thorp Creek trail on the left (east), in a grassy meadow. Ford Hurricane Creek (cold and fast early in the season), cross the wide cobbled wash of Twin Creek without losing the tread, then climb steep switchbacks through burned forest and blowdown to Thorp Creek Meadows below Sacajawea. Fill up on water here: it is the last reliable source until you are back down at Hurricane Creek.
current.descent: From Chief Joseph Mountain there is no trail back to Hurricane Creek. Descend the rocky ridge and then steep forest west toward the creek, through burned regrowth, dense brush, deadfall that collapses underfoot and small cliff bands. Hurricane Creek must then be forded to regain the Hurricane Creek Trail, which leads back down-valley to the trailhead. Allow several hours for the final mile or two; this is often the slowest part of the day.

name: Krag Peak Traverse
beta: Walk the East Eagle Trail up the valley for about 1.5 mi, then leave it and head right into the steep basin on Krag Peak's west side. The route follows a steep, loose rib splitting a pair of big drainages. Keep to the rib's crest instead of dropping into the gullies on either side. Expect sections of exposure with big loose blocks, and test every hold. The rib tops out on the west (northwest) summit. From there, traverse the crest to the slightly higher east summit, then continue along the ridge crest before descending the rubbly slopes toward Crater Lake. From the lake, pick up the Little Kettle Creek Trail and follow its many switchbacks back down to the East Eagle Trailhead.
overview: A steep, off-trail loop over both summits of Krag Peak, a double-topped peak in the southern Wallowas that rises about 4,500 ft above East Fork Eagle Creek in roughly a mile. You climb a loose rib on the west side to the lower west summit, cross to the higher east summit, follow the crest, and drop to Crater Lake to return by trail. The scrambling is Class 3 on loose rock with some exposure; the trail miles at either end are straightforward.

current.approach: From the East Eagle Trailhead, follow the East Eagle Trail (#1910) up the East Fork Eagle Creek valley for about 1.5 mi to where the route leaves the trail and heads right, up the steep basin on Krag Peak's west side.
current.descent: From the east summit, follow the ridge crest and then descend rubbly, loose slopes toward Crater Lake. At the lake, join the Little Kettle Creek Trail (#1945) and follow it down more than 25 switchbacks, through open, sun-exposed slopes that can be overgrown in places, back to the East Eagle Trailhead.

name: Three Sisters Traverse
beta: South Sister (10,358'): from the Devils Lake Trailhead, climb the South Sister climbers' trail through forest and onto the open plateau, then continue north up the South Ridge on steep scree, skirting the Lewis Glacier's moraine lake on its west side, to the crater rim and around to the summit - a Class 2 walk-up on loose volcanic rock. Leave the summit down the Northwest Ridge (Class 2, snow early and scree late; the Eugene Glacier snowfield lies along its flank) and drop north toward the saddle with Middle Sister above Camp Lake. Middle Sister (10,047'): climb the South Ridge, mostly big talus (Class 2), to the summit, then descend the North Ridge (Class 2-3; it can hold steep snow or ice early in the season) and follow the upper edge of the Collier Glacier to the saddle between Prouty Point and North Sister. North Sister (10,085'): scramble loose slopes onto the South Ridge and follow climbers' paths that alternate between west-side ledges and the east side at gaps. Below the summit pinnacle, cross the Terrible Traverse - a steep, exposed snowfield with a nasty runout in early and mid-summer, an easy Class 3 scree crossing once melted out - then turn up into the Bowling Alley, a steep, loose gully between the pinnacle's horns. Its headwall is easy but loose Class 4; above it, Class 2-3 leads to the summit block. Reverse the pinnacle and ridge to the Prouty Point saddle to start the exit.
overview: A long point-to-point link-up of all three Sisters, running south to north from the Devils Lake Trailhead over South Sister, Middle Sister and North Sister and finishing at the Pole Creek Trailhead, so it needs a car shuttle. South and Middle Sister are non-technical scrambles and snow climbs, but North Sister comes last and is the crux: loose Class 3-4 rock, the exposed Terrible Traverse and the rockfall-prone Bowling Alley to its summit pinnacle. Most parties do it as one very long day; some split it with a night between the peaks.

current.approach: From the Devils Lake Trailhead (5,450') on the Cascade Lakes Highway, cross the highway and follow the South Sister climbers' trail up through forest. After about 1.5 miles it leaves the trees and crosses a trail junction onto the open plateau below South Sister's South Ridge, which leads straight up to the summit.
current.descent: From North Sister, reverse the ridge to the saddle between North Sister and Prouty Point, then descend the lateral moraine on the north side of the Hayden Glacier and follow a climbers' path down beside a creek to the Pole Creek Trail. Cross Soap Creek and follow the trail past the Green Lakes junction and through the old burn - shadeless and dusty by late summer - to the Pole Creek Trailhead (5,300'). From the Prouty Point saddle to the car is roughly 5 miles and 1,600' of descent.
rack: 2-4 pickets (when the Terrible Traverse holds snow)
current.pro_needs: Pickets for the Terrible Traverse while it is snow; slings to back up or replace fixed rappel anchors in the Bowling Alley.
current.rope_note: A single 60 m rope reaches from rappel anchors near the top of the Bowling Alley. Many parties rope up for the Terrible Traverse while it holds snow; late season, confident parties climb and downclimb North Sister unroped.

name: Amplified Heat
beta: Begin at the foot of the big dihedral, follow the green-stained streak into the crack, then finish up the face overhead to reach the belay bolts.
overview: Climbs the big dihedral along a green-stained streak before switching to a crack, then the wall above, ending at a bolted belay. The second pitch is shared with a neighbouring route. Described as excellent.

current.location: base of the giant open book

name: Boston
beta:
First pitch: climb the face to a notch, mount it, shift left and then angle rightward, clipping a pair of bolts, to a comfortable treed ledge.

Second pitch: ascend rightward along a big flake, traverse over its top toward a little tree, then follow the dark streak directly to the summit.
overview: Two pitches: a face to the notch and a couple of bolts leading to a treed ledge, then a big flake and a dark streak to the top. Rated excellent.

current.location: beneath a notch in the arch, starting right of the ramp

name: Deep Prok
beta: Head directly up to the bolt beneath the arch, enter the arch from its left side, and surmount the bulge via its crack; two further bolts lead to the top.
overview: Heads straight for a bolt beneath the arch, steps left inside it, surmounts a bulge that has a crack, and finishes past two more bolts.

current.area_walk_in: Take the Echo Canyon trail through the saddle between Main Dome and Little Dome, drop down the draw and cross the boulders, then follow the trail that loops around the dome to the wall's base.
current.descent: rappel from anchors to the right

name: Dome Driver
beta:
First pitch: angle leftward up to a tree set into the overlap, mantel it and clip a pair of bolts, then join the long right-rising crack-and-ledge line and stop at a belay beside another tree under the Boston flake.

Second pitch: climb the flake, step left onto the black streak, and follow that streak to the belay bolts; it is exposed and offers little protection.
overview: Pitch one angles leftward to a tree, crosses the overlap with two bolts, and joins a long diagonal ledge. Pitch two climbs a flake onto a bare dark streak with no gear, to a bolted belay. Exposed, runout, a classic of the area.

current.location: from a boulder next to Boston, below the highest section of the overlap

name: Easier Than It Looks
beta:
First pitch: follow solid holds up a series of corners onto a ramp that slants rightward, and stop beside Fatman Flake, under a steeper headwall, to belay.

Second pitch: go up the flake, veer leftward onto a ledge, then keep climbing easy rock where no gear is available, or move left to belay at the summit. A modest set of nuts and cams is enough.
overview: Starts on boulders. A first pitch of solid holds in corners reaches a ramp and a flake belay; the second pitch gains the flake, moves leftward onto a ledge, and finishes on easy terrain with no protection or by a leftward traverse to the top.

current.detailed_rack: small selection of wires and cams

name: Edge of Night
beta: Ascend the centre of the hourglass-shaped flake toward the shallow arch (small gear suits the arch crack), then edge up the thinner face above, clip a bolt, and finish straight onto a ledge for belaying.
overview: Ascends the centre of the hourglass-like flake into a shallow arch, then a bold stretch of 5.8 to a bolt, finishing up to a ledge belay.

current.area_walk_in: Take the Echo Canyon trail through the saddle between Main Dome and Little Dome, drop down the draw and cross the boulders, then follow the trail that loops around the dome to the wall's base.
current.descent: (no DESCENT section on this route's page)
current.detailed_rack: bring small protection suited to the arch
